related_questions.question: What stage of cancer is metastasized?
related_questions.snippet: Cancer that spreads from where it started to a distant part of the body is called metastatic cancer. For many types of cancer, it is also called stage 4 cancer. The process by which cancer cells spread to other parts of the body is called metastasis.

related_questions.question: How long will you live with metastatic cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Metastatic cancer survival rates For example, the five-year survival rate for metastatic lung cancer is 9%. This means that 9% of people diagnosed with metastatic lung cancer are still alive five years later. Meanwhile, the five-year survival rate of metastatic breast cancer is 30% for women and 19% for men.

related_questions.question: What organ is first in metastasis?
related_questions.snippet: Initially, nearby lymph nodes are struck early. The lungs, liver, brain, and bones are the most common metastasis locations from solid tumors. Although advanced cancer may cause pain, it is often not the first symptom. Some patients, however, do not show any symptoms.

related_questions.question: What does it mean if a doctor says that your cancer has metastasized?
related_questions.snippet: Doctors usually use the term metastatic cancer to describe cancer that has spread to distant organs or distant lymph nodes (called distant metastases). The most common places for distant metastases are the bones, brain, liver and lungs.

text_blocks.snippet: Metastatic cancer refers to cancer that has spread from its original site (primary tumor) to other parts of the body.
snippet_highlighted_words: cancer that has spread from its original site (primary tumor) to other parts of the body

text_blocks.snippet: When cancer cells break away from the primary tumor, they can travel through the bloodstream or lymphatic system to settle in other organs or tissues. These cancer cells can then grow and form new tumors, known as metastases.
Metastatic cancer is typically more advanced and difficult to treat than the primary tumor. It can spread to various organs, including the bones, liver, lungs, brain, and lymph nodes.
The presence of metastases is often used to indicate the stage of cancer and to guide treatment decisions.
